id: iterated-simple-wreath-bounded-commutator-width-proof
kind: route
title: The bottom layer is the unique minimal normal subgroup, so Lucchini--Menegazzo bounds generation by depth-one data, and Nikolov--Segal bounds commutator width
target: iterated-simple-wreath-bounded-commutator-width

---

**Item 1.** Induct on `d`. `W_1 = T_1` is perfect. `W_d` is generated by the root copy of `T_1` together
with the subtree copies of the depth-`(d-1)` towers at the children, all of them perfect. A group
generated by perfect subgroups is perfect.

**Item 2.** `B = prod_(v) T_d(v)`, over the vertices `v` just above the leaves, is normal.
- *Every nontrivial normal `N` meets `B`.* Let `g in N`, `g != 1`.
  - If `g` fixes every vertex above the leaves, then `g in B`.
  - Otherwise `g(v) != v` for some such `v`. Take `u in B` supported at `v` with label `t != 1`. Then
    `[g, u] = g u g^-1 u^-1` has label `t^-1` at `v`, so it is nontrivial and lies in `N ∩ B`.
- *`N` contains `B`.* `N ∩ B` is normal in `B = T_d^k`, so it is the product of some of the factors: the
  normal subgroups of a direct product of nonabelian simple groups are the partial products. It is
  invariant under `W`, which permutes the factors transitively because every `T_i` is transitive. So
  `N ∩ B = B`.
- So `B` is the unique minimal normal subgroup. `W/B` acts on the tree with the leaves removed, and it is
  the depth-`(d-1)` tower.

**Item 3.** `W_d` is noncyclic, being nonabelian. By item 2 and
`lucchini-menegazzo-unique-minimal-normal-generation`, `d(W_d) = max(2, d(W_(d-1)))`. By induction
`d(W_d) = max(2, d(T_1))`. Since `T_1 <= Sym(m)`, a chain of proper subgroups gives
`d(T_1) <= log_2 |T_1| <= log_2 m!`.

**Item 4.** `W` is `delta(m)`-generated (item 3) and perfect (item 1), so `[W, W] = W`. By
`nikolov-segal-uniform-commutator-width`, every element is a product of at most `c(m) := f(delta(m))`
commutators.
